parts.note: fly is slang for knowing or sharp-witted
something cut into two equal parts is in halves

explanation.surface: Performers who are wise to the fact that the script has two parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly-halves are rugby players, the stand-off positions; 'Players' is plural, matching the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the fly-half is the backline player who links scrum and threequarters, so a team's pair of them are players.

definitions.meaning: natural powers or talents of the mind
a university is divided into teaching divisions such as arts or law, noted features of any campus

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both mental powers or gifts and the departments into which a university is organised.

definitions.meaning: Edward ..., eighteenth-century English poet of Night Thoughts
the offspring of an animal, a brood or litter

explanation.definitionFit: Edward Young wrote Night Thoughts, and an animal's offspring collectively are its brood.

indicators.note: the box word holds the copper symbol inside it

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box for goods
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a box holds copper coins and is told they are correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying that's right confirms something is correct, exact or true.

clue.text: French writer shows what makes current on river

parts.note: the volt is the unit of electrical pressure that drives a current
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A French author demonstrates how electricity is generated beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The AIRE is a river in Yorkshire, England; 'on' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire was the pen name of the eighteenth-century French philosopher and satirist who wrote Candide.

parts.note: not a portrait of a writer but a comparison a writer uses, likening one thing to another with like or as

explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech comparing two things explicitly is a stylistic device authors employ to show resemblance.

clue.text: Daisy appears to become sickly looking

parts.note: go means become, as in go pale
wan means pale and ill-looking

explanation.surface: A flower seems to be wilting and going pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Gowan is a Scottish word for the daisy; 'appears' only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish dialect the common white field flower is called a gowan.

parts.note: a sounder is the collective noun for a herd of pigs, so the noises such a herd makes

explanation.surface: Noises made by something more reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs make low guttural noises, and a sounder is a group of swine.

clue.text: Immediately after which, we hope, NUR members assembled

indicators.note: the letters are gathered and put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Trade unionists gather in hope of a result, after which things happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR was Britain's National Union of Railwaymen; 'members assembled' pictures them meeting, but 'assembled' rearranges WE HOPE and NUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction introduces what happened straight after and as a result of something.

parts.note: there were nine Muses, so a piece written for that many players

explanation.surface: A tune dedicated to the goddesses of the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for nine instruments or voices is so named, and the classical Muses numbered nine.

indicators.note: the word for advice is said out loud, giving a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: counsel means advice

explanation.surface: Good, solid advice is offered to a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A council is a deliberative body, an assembly of people meeting to govern or advise.

clue.text: Girl gets a remuneration but no food, maybe

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are rearranged once the food word's letters are taken away from them

parts.note: a ration is an allowance of food

explanation.surface: A girl is paid but given nothing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of RATION out of A REMUNERATION and rearrange what is left: there is no anagram word, so the remainder simply has to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Maureen is a girl's name, an Irish form of Mary.

indicators.note: coming back means the word for royal is read backwards

parts.note: regal means of or fit for kings

explanation.surface: A royal beverage returns to fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light bottom-fermented beer, a common drink.

definitions.meaning: a rented plot of land where a person digs and grows vegetables, playing on diggings as lodgings

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an apportioned portion and a small rented garden plot for growing vegetables, common in Britain.

clue.text: A rum time to gather the unripe portions !

indicators.note: the letters are collected together and reassembled in a different order

explanation.surface: A strange moment to harvest fruit that is not yet ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the anagram signal, but the whole of A RUM TIME is the fodder and 'to gather' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Immature fruit has not yet developed fully, just as unripe fruit is not ready to eat.

clue.text: Smuggled spirits found in a lighter

definitions.meaning: the glow given off by the moon, something that lights up the night

explanation.definitionFit: The word means illicit liquor and also the light of the moon at night.

indicators.note: letters found inside the novel's title, running across both words

explanation.surface: Smollett's novel Peregrine Pickle has a bold cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic describes grand, heroic deeds on the scale of an epic poem.

clue.text: Ranch hand finds McNeal arranged about a race

the letters of the name are set out in another order

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.definitionFit: A cattleman tends or raises livestock, as a hand on a ranch does.

clue.text: Fellow sportsman to make the last move

definitions.meaning: in chess, to play the winning checkmate

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a companion in play, and split it reads as playing checkmate, the final move.

parts.note: reads like a job or concert booking but means asking someone to marry

definitions.meaning: a try or go at something
the bang of a gun firing

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a try at something and also the discharge of a gun, heard as a report.

clue.text: Musical instrument-many learn it for diversion

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: diverting the letters sends them into a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of people take up a woodwind instrument as a hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument.

definitions.meaning: read as mite amid ship, a small thing inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: a mite in the middle of SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: To smite is to hit hard, and the second reading places a small creature inside the steamship abbreviation.

parts.note: a merry ... is a clown, and one saint of that name is patron of Scotland

explanation.surface: Which holy figure is the jolly one?
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is called a merry andrew, and Scotland's patron saint shares the name.

parts.note: banknotes paid to keep someone silent rather than soft musical notes

explanation.surface: Soft musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe paid to keep a secret is a payment for silence.

parts.note: a bounder is a cad but also anything that hops, so the apt words telling it to go away

explanation.surface: The right way to send a cad packing.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt slang order to go away suits a hopping creature such as a kangaroo.

clue.text: Go seeking plunder in front of ship — money

parts.note: the prow is the bow of a ship
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pirate stands at the bow hunting for loot and cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam stealthily in search of prey or spoils.

parts.note: to dock is to cut short, as is to lop

explanation.surface: A choice between a ship's deck and its dock.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: OT character Sarah in the "wilds of Moab

definitions.meaning: a wood is made up of many of these
a famous song setting Joyce Kilmer's poem about them

explanation.definitionFit: A wood consists of many timber plants, and Kilmer's poem became a well-known song of that title.

definitions.text: OK for roulette players but : 'not for motorists

parts.note: a roulette wheel must turn freely, but a car's wheels turning without grip is bad
